thread:
Alex: heads-up — saw a production incident where a bursty streaming job ate the org token bucket and caused chat endpoints to 429. anyone seen this pattern before?
Priya: seen it once during a demo loadtest. streaming clients keep long-lived connections and token accounting is weird.
Sam: are we charging streaming the same token cost as chat? streaming has steady per-second burn instead of per-response. that compounds.
Jordan: yeah, current model: per-token accounting is shared by org-key. streaming requests increment token count continuously while open.
Mei: that sounds expected but problematic. we should isolate burst capacity for streaming so a long session doesn't block short chat calls.
Alex: proposal: per-endpoint ephemeral burst bucket (size configurable) + fallback to org shared bucket once ephemeral depleted. ephemeral should refill slowly and cap per-conn.
Priya: +1. can we enforce per-conn cap too? e.g. streaming_conn_max_burst = 1024 tokens, refill 1 token/sec. prevents single client from draining.
Sam: implementation detail: two buckets per key: endpoint:<key>:streaming:burst and endpoint:<key>:shared. token consumption prefers burst, then falls back. but there's race if both drained simultaneously.
Jordan: we also need a handoff window so when streaming is idle we don't immediately transfer debt to shared. current abrupt handoff causes sudden spike on chat. idea: handoff_window_seconds = 60 — only start charging shared after sustained consumption or conn close.
Mei: on observability side we need dashboards: per-key burn rate, endpoint burn, handoff events, and a cross-impact graph (streaming -> chat 429 correlation). otherwise debugging is painful.
Alex: agreed. also add a metric 'quota.handoff.count' and 'quota.handoff.reason' labels.
Priya: what about rate-limit headers? make 429s from shared bucket include X-Quota-Status to hint to clients (can show streaming overload).
Sam: config prototype (for the console/config API):
```
{
  "policy_name": "per-key-endpoint-burst-v2",
  "endpoints": {
    "streaming": {
      "burst_size": 2048,
      "refill_rate_per_sec": 2,
      "conn_max_burst": 1024,
      "handoff_window_seconds": 60,
      "fallback_to_shared": true
    },
    "chat": {"burst_size": 512, "refill_rate_per_sec": 5}
  },
  "shared": {"org_bucket_size": 20000}
}
```
Jordan: sounds reasonable. need to check CPU cost of maintaining per-conn state for all streaming sockets though. could be heavy at 100k conns. maybe only track active conns above threshold.
Mei: telemetry-wise we should sample handoff traces at 1% to Sentry-like pipeline to inspect request flows. also add a console heatmap for 'per-endpoint burn over time' with hover to show top keys.
Alex: rollout plan: feature-flag behind devex quota-ui + staged enable for small set of orgs, observe handoff events and 429 reduction.
deploy-bot: rolled out quota-endpoint-burst-v2 to staging at 2026-03-18T10:12:01Z — https://deploys.internal/redwood/12345 :rocket:
Priya: one more: UX in console should let customers tune per-endpoint burst and show estimated cost impact (tokens/sec -> $/hr). otherwise they'll be confused.
Sam: ok I'll mock the server-side changes, Jordan will do performance testing, Mei will add dashboards. can we sync tomorrow 9am PT?
Alex: 9am PT works. thanks all. :+1:
Mei: added an initial dashboard card prototype to the staging workspace — /dashboards/quotas/endpoint-burn (visibility: eng-platform).
Jordan: I'll start load tests to validate conn state overhead and refine conn-tracking heuristics.
Alex: wrap-up: implement ephemeral per-endpoint burst, handoff window, headers for 429, dashboards, gradual rollout.
Priya: noted. I'll draft console UI copy for the new controls.
__notes: Followed agents.md: single string thread, short messages, includes bot and code snippet.
